findings.title: Freeze the Controller, Defrost the Food: Uncovering Vulnerabilities in Danfoss Refrigeration Controllers
findings.summary_md: Claroty Team82 found multiple vulnerabilities in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controller, including a hidden code-of-the-day authentication bypass (CVE-2025-41450), command injection leading to remote code execution (CVE-2025-41451), and an Nginx configuration injection (CVE-2025-41452). Internet-wide scanning showed 2,765 exposed AK-SM 800A management interfaces. Danfoss addressed the flaws in firmware version R4.3.1.

findings.title: Hackers force French supermarket fridges to heat up to 50C in 'unprecedented' cyber-attack
findings.summary_md: Hundreds of Intermarche and Cooperative U shops in France were hit, with freezers forced up to 50 degrees Celsius and food discarded, and there were fears Dutch chains were also affected. This was the first wave of the campaign, three weeks before the November multi-country wave.

findings.title: Incident de securite ciblant les controleurs a distance des installations de refrigeration
findings.summary_md: CERT-FR warned of numerous compromises of remote refrigeration controllers, naming Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series plus Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. It advised removing internet exposure, restoring access only through a VPN or protected network, and performing a factory reset plus reconfiguration for compromised end-of-life devices.

findings.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
findings.summary_md: Attackers compromised Danfoss controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets, forcing defrost cycles and causing food losses. CERT-FR had issued its alert on October 12 naming Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series devices.

findings.title: Supermarket Refrigeration Attack Widens to Copeland, Dixell Controllers
findings.summary_md: Around 700 French supermarkets were affected, with no group claiming responsibility. CERT-FR first warned on October 12 of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC compromises and added Copeland XWEB and Dixell XWEB systems a day later. Copeland acknowledged a vulnerability, while most affected Danfoss devices were end-of-life AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355 units no longer patched.

findings.title: Cold Chain, Open Control: Exposed Refrigeration Systems Reveal Global Risk
findings.summary_md: Forescout Vedere Labs identified 12,976 internet-exposed refrigeration service observations across 10 product groups, represented by 6,017 distinct public IP addresses in 99 countries and territories. The French incident affected more than 700 supermarkets, and exposed management interfaces create a global cold-chain risk beyond retail.

findings.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
findings.summary_md: Freezers in supermarkets across Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and other countries were pushed to around 50 degrees Celsius overnight. Belgian firm Sabcobel said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, the same method as the October French incident, and a Danfoss spokesperson said at least 17 Dutch businesses were hit.

findings.title: Over 100 European Stores Hit as Supermarket Fridge Attacks Return
findings.summary_md: More than 100 stores across Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden saw refrigeration units heat to as high as 50 degrees Celsius overnight November 1-2. Lupovis recorded suspicious activity against Danfoss AK-SM sensors from October 20 to 30 peaking October 26 using factory-default credentials, and Censys counted 138 exposed StoreView instances in Belgium, 51 in the Netherlands and 50 in Sweden.
